rounds.proof_sketch: For dim=1: inner_size=256, grid.y=(256+255)/256=1, max inner_idx=255. For dim=0: inner_size=65536, grid.y=256, max inner_idx=65535. In both cases, max(inner_idx) = inner_size-1, so the condition inner_idx==inner_size is never true. The mutation from '>=' to '>' only differs when inner_idx==inner_size, which is unreachable.
rounds.survival_reason: The kernel launch configuration ensures that the maximum inner_idx equals inner_size-1. With block_size=256 and inner_size being 256 (for dim=1) or 65536 (for dim=0), the grid is sized exactly to cover all valid indices without overflow. The changed boundary check from 'inner_idx >= inner_size' to 'inner_idx > inner_size' only differs at the single point inner_idx==inner_size, which no thread ever reaches. This is an architectural property of the fixed shape [16,256,256] where dimensions divide evenly by the block size.
rounds.kill_strategy: This mutant is unkillable under the fixed-shape contract. Killing it would require either: (1) changing the input shape to have an inner dimension that is not a perfect multiple arrangement with block_size=256, or (2) using dim=2 which would set inner_size=1 and expose the boundary bug. Both require configuration changes that are prohibited.
rounds.recommendations: When testing boundary guard mutations in GPU kernels, verify that the boundary case is actually reachable given the fixed launch configuration. Mutations on guards like 'idx >= N' vs 'idx > N' are only observable when some thread has idx==N, which depends on the relationship between grid dimensions, block size, and data dimensions.
